edges.description: Truncating alleles are expected to remove one functional copy of WBP11, halving the available splicing factor. Direct measurement of WBP11 protein in patient tissue has not been reported; the edge rests on the variant class and on the heterozygous null mouse.
Reduced WBP11 impairs spliceosome function, producing intron retention and exon skipping across many transcripts.
Mis-splicing of TUBGCP6, a core gamma-tubulin ring complex component, lowers TUBGCP6 protein and impairs centriole duplication.
Splicing defects in developmental gene programs are proposed to disturb morphogenesis of the axial skeleton, heart, foregut, kidney and limbs. The specific causal targets are unknown.
Proposed link from centriole duplication failure to reduced brain growth, by analogy with other spliceosome disorders; not tested for WBP11.
Abnormal axial skeletal development produces vertebral segmentation and fusion anomalies.
Abnormal heart development produces septal and other structural cardiac defects.
Abnormal foregut separation produces esophageal atresia with or without tracheoesophageal fistula.
Abnormal kidney development produces renal agenesis or hypodysplasia.
Limb defects are proposed to follow from abnormal limb development; the zebrafish shows fin hypoplasia, but no mammalian limb defect has been reported.
Sprengel anomaly (failure of scapular descent) often accompanies cervical vertebral segmentation defects and is presumed to share their developmental origin.
The heterozygous null mouse reproduces the axial skeletal, renal and esophageal malformations of the human disorder.
edges.limitations: The heterozygous mouse lacks the cardiac defects seen in patients, so it models only part of the malformation spectrum.

edges.description: Morphants show multi-system defects, including the cardiac component absent from the mouse.
edges.limitations: Morpholino knockdown is a transient reduction rather than a heterozygous null genotype, can have off-target effects, and fin hypoplasia is only an analogue of mammalian limb defects. The authors describe the model as partially recapitulating the human disorder.

nodes.description: Structural heart defects, ventricular septal defect being the one named, in 8 of 13 postnatal cases. Cardiac malformation is the dominant prenatal finding (3 of 5 fetuses).

evidence.reference_title: Prenatal and postnatal manifestations of WBP11-related disorder in Chinese patients: expanding the phenotypic and mutational spectrum.
evidence.snippet: Notably, prenatal cases predominantly presented with cardiac malformations, whereas vertebral anomalies, common postnatally, were absent prenatally, suggesting age-dependent phenotypic evolution.

nodes.description: Abnormal development of the axial skeleton, heart, tracheoesophageal foregut, kidney and limbs, producing the VACTERL-spectrum malformations. Heterozygous null mice show axial skeletal, renal and esophageal defects but no cardiac defects; morphant zebrafish show cardiac, vascular, notochord, fin and renal-marker defects.

nodes.description: Reported alleles are predominantly nonsense, frameshift and canonical splice-site variants predicted to cause loss of function, with a smaller number of predicted damaging missense variants. They occur de novo or are inherited from mildly affected or unaffected carriers.

evidence.reference_title: Heterozygous loss of WBP11 function causes multiple congenital defects in humans and mice.
evidence.snippet: Here, we report novel heterozygous predicted loss-of-function (LoF) and predicted damaging missense variants in the WW domain binding protein 11 (WBP11) gene in seven unrelated families with a variety of overlapping congenital malformations, including cardiac, vertebral, tracheo-esophageal, renal and limb defects.

evidence.snippet: whole genome sequencing presented a de novo novel WBP11 heterozygous pathogenic variant, with frameshift resulting in a loss of function.

nodes.description: WBP11 is required for centriole duplication through correct splicing of TUBGCP6. Centriole defects are linked to microcephaly and growth restriction in other spliceosomopathies and may contribute to those features here. This has been shown in cultured cells, not in patient tissue.

evidence.reference_title: WBP11 is required for splicing the TUBGCP6 pre-mRNA to promote centriole duplication.
evidence.snippet: WBP11 depletion causes centriole duplication defects, in part by causing a rapid decline in the level of TUBGCP6.

nodes.description: Limb defects, in 5 of 13 postnatal cases. The individual limb lesions are not described in the cached abstracts.

nodes.description: Loss of WBP11 causes retention of roughly 200 introns in human cells and widespread intron retention and exon skipping in zebrafish embryos. The affected transcripts include genes for cardiac function, angiogenesis, skeletal patterning, fin and kidney development. Which mis-spliced targets drive which malformations is not established.

nodes.description: Reduced WBP11 dosage. WBP11 is a nuclear-speckle and spliceosome component that activates pre-mRNA splicing and also binds protein phosphatase 1. Complete loss is incompatible with development (Wbp11 null mouse embryos die before E8.5), while heterozygous loss reduces viability and causes malformations.

evidence.reference_title: Heterozygous loss of WBP11 function causes multiple congenital defects in humans and mice.
evidence.snippet: WBP11 encodes a component of the spliceosome with the ability to activate pre-messenger RNA splicing.

evidence.snippet: Finally, we found that SIPP1 is also a component of the spliceosomes and that a SIPP1-fragment inhibits splicing catalysis by nuclear extracts independent of its ability to interact with PP1.

nodes.description: Canonical acceptor splice-site variant found in a fetus with isolated femoral shortening. RNA from amniocytes showed only 4% aberrant splicing (c.1310del, p.Gly437Glufs*6), so this canonical splice-site variant retains most normal splicing and should not be classified pathogenic on sequence grounds alone.

evidence.reference_title: Prenatal and postnatal manifestations of WBP11-related disorder in Chinese patients: expanding the phenotypic and mutational spectrum.
evidence.snippet: Crucially, RNA analysis of amniocytes carrying the c.1310-1G > A variant revealed only 4% aberrant splicing (c.1310del, p.Gly437Glufs*6), explaining the mild fetal phenotype of isolated femoral shortening

nodes.description: CRISPR-Cas9 null allele. Homozygous embryos die before E8.5. Heterozygotes are under-represented because of embryonic and postnatal death, are small, and have axial skeletal, renal and esophageal defects; cardiac defects are not reported.

Translation-blocking morpholino knockdown, validated by Western blot and rescued by wbp11 mRNA co-injection. About 70% of morphants are malformed, with cardiac, vascular, notochord and spinal, fin and kidney-marker defects and widespread mis-splicing.
